sources.role: original researcher with competing commercial product
findings: Researcher reports two vulnerabilities disclosed August12 and fixed within eight days.
Researcher identifies distinct fixed versions for desktop and CLI; one installed CLI version does not establish both fixes.

sources.role: independent reporting including attributed provider response
findings: The September21 update includes an OpenAI spokesperson saying both issues were addressed in August.
This is provider acknowledgement reported by the outlet, not an independent patch test.

correctionToEarlierAssessment: There is now a located attributed provider acknowledgement in the independent article, beyond the researcher claim alone. Exact fixed build thresholds remain attributed to Accomplish; no independent exploit or patch reproduction performed.
readerScope: People using Codex coding tools; no evidence ordinary ChatGPT chat users are affected by these two defects. Explain sandbox as limits on software access before naming technical components.

productionBrief.question: Does this report mean my AI chat escaped, or is there a specific coding-tool update I need?
sequence: Identify Codex coding tool and separate this from ordinary ChatGPT chat and unrelated AISI incidents.
Explain that a sandbox restricts what a tool can access; a defect in enforcement can bypass those limits.
Report two distinct vulnerabilities, dated disclosure and provider acknowledgement of August remediation.
Scope update advice to the relevant desktop/CLI installation, without equating app-bundled CLI number to app build.
Keep researcher commercial interest and absence of independent patch testing visible.
excluded: Exploit code, payloads or reproduction steps
Claim all AI or all ChatGPT users affected
Claim every current installation is patched
Treat developer settings as universal consumer UI guidance
